items.title: Türkiye-Israel tensions deepen over Syria, Netanyahu Interpol request
items.description: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said on Saturday that it fired towards a militant who was in the final stages of preparing an attack in southern Syria, citing threats to its soldiers, days after Israeli strikes on a Syrian airbase near the Turkish border. The latest strike took place as tensions between Israel and Türkiye have intensified following Ankara's request for an Interpol Red Notice against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Analysts view the Interpol move as a reflection of the widening rift between the two countries in recent years, but see the action as largely symbolic in nature. Rising Türkiye-Israel tensions over Syria Türkiye has requested the issuance of an Interpol Red Notice for Netanyahu following an arrest warrant issued against him last month on a charge of "genocide." The Interpol request was made in connection with an ongoing Turkish criminal case over the interception of activists aboard the Global Sumud Flotilla, which set sail from Türkiye in May in a renewed attempt to break Israel's blockade of Gaza, according to Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek on Friday. The flotilla was intercepted by Israel, and those on board were subsequently deported. The Israeli Prime Minister's Office responded by accusing Türkiye of "hypocrisy" and referring to its President Recep Tayyip Erdogan as an "antisemitic dictator," saying Erdogan was seeking to extend what it called his "aggression" against Israel into Syria. The statement added that Israel would continue to act against what it described as threats to its security. Türkiye's Communications Directorate hit back, describing the Israeli statement targeting Erdogan as "outrageous ravings" devoid of historical fact and political seriousness. It accused the Netanyahu government of using "cheap politics" for electoral gain and seeking to portray Türkiye as a new threat, warning that efforts to escalate tensions for domestic political competition posed risks to regional and global peace and stability. The diplomatic exchanges followed Israeli airstrikes on Tuesday targeting the Abu al-Duhur military airport in Idlib Province in northwestern Syria, which caused material damage but no casualties. The airport, a major Syrian airbase, is situated near routes linking parts of Idlib, Aleppo and Hama provinces. Israel said the airstrike was aimed at preventing what it described as a potential Turkish military deployment at the Syrian airbase, which it said would pose a threat to its security. Ankara has firmly denied any such deployment. On Saturday, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said in a statement that the Tuesday strikes on the Syrian military airport were in response to "clear intelligence" received about Türkiye's intentions to carry out actions there that would endanger Israel's security. Katz said the Israeli military had recommended several times to attack the airport, rejecting claims by the Israeli opposition that the operation was carried out for political reasons ahead of Israel's general elections on October 27. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar said on Saturday that while tensions with Türkiye remain high over the Syria issue, Israel has no intention of escalating tensions and "always prioritizes" diplomatic solutions. He also stressed that Israel will never accept Türkiye establishing a base in Syria. Syria condemns Israel 'in strongest terms' Syrian state news agency SANA reported on Saturday that a civilian was injured when an Israeli drone targeted a car in the town of Beit Jinn in southwestern Damascus. The injured person was transferred to a hospital. The report did not identify the person targeted or provide details about the circumstances surrounding the strike. Following the attack, Syria's foreign affairs authority condemned "in the strongest terms" what it described as the Israeli occupation forces' targeting of a civilian vehicle, saying the attack resulted in several injuries among civilians. The authority said the attack constituted "a blatant violation" of Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity and a flagrant breach of international law, adding that it came amid repeated Israeli attacks on Syrian territory. The Britain-based Syrian Observatory for Human Rights said it had documented 57 Israeli attacks on Syrian territory since the beginning of 2026, including six air attacks and 51 ground attacks. Tensions 'largely at diplomatic, rhetorical levels' Analysts said the deterioration of Turkish-Israeli relations is expected to remain largely at the diplomatic and rhetorical levels, and since Türkiye is a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), it seems unlikely that Israel would engage in a direct military confrontation with a NATO country. Both Türkiye and Israel are major regional powers, and the United States would not like to see a serious conflict between the pair, they said. Canan Tercan, a Turkish political analyst at Istanbul Aydin University, said Israel's concerns over Türkiye's growing role in Syria were central to the latest tensions. "Türkiye's presence in Syria for training purposes is entirely at the request of the Syrian government," Tercan said, noting that Ankara has no territorial ambitions and seeks to support Syria's unitary state structure. Tercan also linked the escalating rhetoric to Israel's domestic political environment, saying Netanyahu faces increasing pressure ahead of the country's October election and may seek to maintain a hard-line security narrative. In response to Türkiye's request for an Interpol Red Notice for Netanyahu, Tercan said the move could raise questions about the international standing of the Israeli prime minister. "The issuance of an international Red Notice is a critically important development," she said, questioning how a political leader sought under an international Red Notice could continue to represent Israel on the international stage. Omer Behram Ozdemir, an analyst at Ibn Haldun University, noted that despite the military provocations, Ankara is likely to maintain a strategy of restraint and focus on long-term institutional rebuilding in Syria rather than direct confrontation. He argued that Israel's strikes are intended to expand the conflict and wear down its counterparts, while Türkiye's continued focus on rebuilding Syria's security institutions could strengthen Ankara's regional influence. (With input from Xinhua)

On August 21, OpenAI announced that it would reduce the benchmark price of GPT-5.6 Sol, a frontier AI model for developers, by more than 20%, effective immediately. The discounted pricing will remain available for three months. At the end of last month, the company also cut prices for several other models, reducing prices for its mid-tier models by 20% and those of its lower-cost models by 80%. items.title: Troops in Rawalpindi okayed for six months
items.description: • Interior ministry says Punjab government requested for army deployment • Order comes over a month before PTI’s planned long march ISLAMABAD: The federal government has authorised the deployment of three companies of the Pakistan Army in Rawalpindi for six months to perform “sensitive security duties” and respond to any unforeseen situation, according to an interior ministry order dated Aug 21. “Pursuant to the request made by the Punjab Home Department […] the federal government, in exercise of the powers conferred under Article 245 of the Cons­titution, is pleased to authorise deployment of three companies of Pakistan Army for sensitive security duties in Rawalpindi to avoid any undesirable situation as well as to respond effectively in any unforeseen situation as per the requirement of the district administration for a period of six months with immediate effect,” the order, a copy of which is available with Dawn , said. Article 245 of the Constitution provides for deployment of the armed forces in aid of civil power. Under the provision, the armed forces may be called upon by the government to assist civilian authorities in maintaining law and order, protecting key installations or responding to emergencies. The deployment has been approved more than a month before the planned Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) march towards Islamabad. The party claims that the Sept 27 long march could draw around two million participants. The deployment also comes amid controversy over implementation of the Supreme Court’s order concerning Mr Khan’s treatment at Shifa International Hospital, with PTI and PML-N trading allegations of contempt of court. Rawalpindi, a garrison city and home to key military and government installations, is frequently placed on heightened security during major political activity, religious events and periods of increased security concern. The city also borders Islamabad and has seen extensive security arrangements during protest movements, elections and large public gatherings. The Punjab Home Department’s request and the subsequent federal approval indicate concerns about potential law and order challenges in the coming months. The order cites the need to prevent any untoward incident and ensure a rapid response, without specifying the exact nature of the threat. District administrations in Punjab have previously sought army assistance under Article 245 during Muharram, election periods, and times of heightened terror alerts. With the deployment approved for an initial period of six months “with immediate effect”, the army units will be placed at the disposal of the Rawalpindi district administration and will perform duties as assigned by the civilian authorities. Published in Dawn, August 23rd, 2026

items.title: VALCO rolling mill opens new frontier for Ghana’s aluminium industry
items.description: The Volta Aluminium Company Limited (VALCO) is positioning itself to move beyond primary aluminium production with the introduction of a continuous casting and rolling mill capable of producing aluminium rods for the domestic electrical cable industry and potentially the international market. The development is expected to strengthen Ghana’s efforts to retain more value from its aluminium resources by supplying locally manufactured intermediate products to downstream industries while reducing their reliance on imported aluminium inputs. The development was disclosed by VALCO’s Finance Director, Sepenu Agbetsise, at the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources’ mid-year performance review and training programme held at the Marriott Hotel in Accra. Mr Agbetsise said the new production line had already undergone industrial testing with two local cable manufacturers, Nexans Kablemetal and Reroy Cables, with the companies providing satisfactory feedback on the samples supplied. He said the development represented an important shift in VALCO’s traditional role as a producer of primary aluminium to a more integrated operation capable of supplying higher-value products to manufacturers. “Hitherto, these companies would have had to import the rod and process it into the various cables that power our homes. Now, VALCO is in a position to supply those directly,” Mr Agbetsise said. Reducing import dependence The new mill could have significant implications for Ghana’s cable and manufacturing industries, which rely substantially on imported aluminium inputs. By producing aluminium rods locally, VALCO could provide manufacturers with a domestic source of an important intermediate product, potentially shortening supply chains and reducing exposure to international freight costs and supply disruptions. The initiative also fits into the broader national ambition to develop an integrated aluminium industry in which Ghana moves beyond exporting or processing primary materials to producing finished and semi-finished aluminium products for both domestic and export markets. The Ghana Integrated Aluminium Development Corporation (GIADEC) is mandated to support development of the value chain, spanning bauxite mining, alumina refining, aluminium smelting and value-added manufacturing. VALCO’s new rolling mill provides an important link in that downstream development by creating an avenue for aluminium produced in Ghana to be converted into products required by other industries. Eye on the export market The company is also looking beyond the domestic market as it seeks to establish the quality and commercial viability of its products internationally. As of June 2026, about 25 metric tonnes of H11 Electrical Conductor (EC) grade aluminium rods had been shipped to Europe for testing. The results were expected by the end of August, according to the information presented at the review. Successful testing and market acceptance could open another avenue for VALCO to supply value-added aluminium products to international customers, strengthening Ghana’s position in the global aluminium market. Alumina remains key challenge Despite the progress on downstream production, VALCO continues to face a major structural challenge: Ghana does not yet have a domestic alumina refinery. The company therefore relies on imported alumina as the key raw material for its smelting operations. Mr Agbetsise said the dependence on imported alumina placed pressure on the company’s working capital because of the time between placing orders, making payments and receiving the material. The arrangement also exposes VALCO to substantial logistics and financing costs. The company effectively bears freight costs when bringing alumina into Ghana and incurs another freight cost when exporting aluminium products. A domestic alumina refinery, therefore, could substantially shorten the supply chain, reduce inventory-in-transit requirements and ease financing and logistics costs. “If we have alumina just at our backyard, we don’t have to pay ahead of time,” Mr Agbetsise said. He explained that local alumina production could reduce both financing requirements and operating costs, improving the competitiveness of the Ghanaian smelting industry. Completing the value chain The development of an alumina refinery has consequently become a critical component of Ghana’s ambition to establish an integrated aluminium industry. The government has been pursuing investors for the establishment of the country’s first alumina refinery, with the refinery, VALCO’s smelting operations and downstream manufacturing viewed as interconnected components of the proposed value chain. For VALCO, the rolling mill provides an opportunity to begin capturing greater value from aluminium even as efforts continue to address the alumina supply gap. The company has identified sectors including construction, automotive, packaging and other manufacturing industries as potential markets where locally produced aluminium products could substitute imported inputs. The emerging production capacity could therefore provide a double benefit: creating a market for locally produced aluminium while giving Ghanaian manufacturers access to locally sourced intermediate materials. With the initial response from domestic cable manufacturers described as satisfactory and overseas testing under way, the new rolling mill could mark an important step in VALCO’s transition from a traditional smelter into a more diversified producer of value-added aluminium products. It also reinforces the broader policy objective of ensuring that Ghana does not merely possess the raw materials and infrastructure for an aluminium industry but captures a greater share of the economic value generated along the entire chain.

items.title: Delta 2027: Why Ogboru will disappoint critics
items.description: By Benson Ndokwe Come 2027 in Delta State, it will be liberation time for Deltans when Chief Great Ovedje Ogboru and his African Democratic Congress (ADC) win the governorship election. Many critics will be taken aback while others will be astounded for somebody who has been written off. And so shall it be as Ogboru is a game changer. The hidden truths about Delta politics will be unveiled. He will set the motion for an accelerated growth of the state while expanding the scope and numbers of those benefiting from the so-called dividends of democracy. Ultimately, it is Deltans that will benefit as the sole aim of Ogboru is to see a greater number of Deltans crossing the poverty index. Deltans must not follow the old and usual pattern of voting during the 2027 elections. They must vote for change enmass, no matter the monetary inducement. Regardless of tribe or religion, Deltans must do the needful in ensuring that Ogboru wins the guber election. It is only when this is done that the gains and benefits of democracy will accrue to the people. Deltans have suffered for too long a time despite its huge oil and gas deposits and also being one of the country’s greatest contributors to our Gross Domestic Product – GDP. It is my fervent prayers that God should open the eyes of Deltans to collectively deviate from their business as usual and vote in Ogboru to kick-start the needed change in the politics of the state. Ogboru knows what the state truly lacks. He knows the inadequacies bedeviling the affairs of the state. Hence, he will pilot the affairs of the state in a pivotal way to attract the much sought-after Foreign Direct Investments. The state shall become a hub of industrialization and manufacturing, which will mean the creation of jobs for our teeming jobless youths. This will, in turn, increase the economic profile of the state. Clusters of cottage industries would be established in all the nooks and crannies of the state. Deltans should come out en masse on election day to make this change possible. It was PLATO who said, “One of the penalties for refusing to participate in politics is that you end up being governed by your inferiors.” Furthermore, Socrates said, “the wise who refuse to rule should prepare to suffer the rules of idiots.” Those who write off Ogboru are doing so at their own peril. His popularity across the length and breadth of Delta state is spreading like a wild fire. This can only be likened to the Finger of God upon his life. Women empowerment shall be given the necessary attention it deserves because of the motherly roles women play in society. The 2027 elections in Delta State should be given a level playing ground for free and fair elections without intimidation and other negative vices as witnessed in past elections. Candidates should be free to canvass for votes from the electorates. If this is done, then it will be goodbye to bad riddance while we welcome the peoples general to take his rightful position in the governance of the state. •Ndokwe lives in Agbor, Delta State The post Delta 2027: Why Ogboru will disappoint critics appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: IHC moved to regulate social media use by children
items.description: • Petitioners seek an effective age-verification mechanism for minors’ accounts • State urged to protect kids from cyberbullying, harassment and harmful online content ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court has been approached seeking directions to the federal government to introduce legislation and a comprehensive regulatory framework to regulate social media use by children under the age of 16. The petition, filed through advocates Muhammad Jalal Haider and Yahya Farid Khawaja, seeks the introduction of an effective age-verification mechanism for social media accounts operated by children under 16. The petitioners have contended that children are increasingly exposed to the harmful effects of social media, including cyberbullying, online harassment, and inappropriate or harmful content, requiring the state to introduce a comprehensive legal and regulatory mechanism for their protection. They have urged the court to direct the government to formulate a policy covering the digital rights, privacy, and mental and physical safety of children, and to impose specific responsibilities on social media platforms to safeguard minors online. The petition has also sought the establishment of a dedicated social media protection and regulatory mechanism to ensure the online safety of children, along with appropriate legislative measures to regulate social media use by persons under 16. The petitioners have referred to protective measures adopted by Australia , France , the United Kingdom , New Zealand, and Spain, where various safeguards, including age restrictions, parental consent, and age-verification mechanisms, have been introduced or proposed to regulate children’s access to social media. The petition relies on the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child and General Comment No. 25, arguing that protecting the best interests of children is not merely a policy objective but a legal obligation of the state. It has been argued that the absence of an effective mechanism for verifying the age of social media users leaves children vulnerable to online risks and prevents meaningful enforcement of safeguards intended for minors. The petitioners have therefore asked the Islamabad High Court to direct the federal government to take appropriate legislative measures to regulate social media use by children under 16 and establish an institutional mechanism responsible for their digital protection. The Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Ministry of Interior, Ministry of Law and Justice, Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), and Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (Pemra) have been made respondents in the petition. Resolution submitted Earlier, a resolution was submitted to the Punjab Assembly last month, seeking a nationwide ban on social media accounts for children under the age of 16 without parental consent, amid growing concerns over cyberbullying, online sexual abuse and digital addiction among the minors. The resolution, moved by Punjab lawmaker Sarah Ahmad, urges the provincial government to recommend to the federal government to introduce comprehensive legislation to regulate children’s access to social media platforms and strengthen online safety measures. It says the protection of children’s physical, mental, psychological and moral development is both a constitutional and moral responsibility of the state, adding that unrestricted access to social media has exposed minors to cyberbullying, online sexual exploitation, inappropriate content, psychological distress, digital addiction and other serious online threats. The resolution recommends that the federal government enact legislation prohibiting children below the age of 16 from creating or maintaining social media accounts unless parental or legal guardian consent is obtained through a reliable age-verification mechanism. It also calls upon the PTA to implement and enforce effective age-verification systems across all social media platforms operating in Pakistan to ensure compliance with the proposed restrictions. The resolution further seeks to make social media companies responsible for complying with child protection standards by requiring them to promptly remove harmful content and provide a safer digital environment for minors. Published in Dawn, August 23rd, 2026

items.title: From tears to laughter, by Funmi Komolafe
items.description: Beloved, gradually we are moving to the end of the month of a new beginning but it does not mean that the manifestation of new things would cease. As Christians, we are aware that the mercy of God never ceases. Lamentations 3 vs.23 ( KJV) “They (mercies) are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness”, Whatever the situation with a person, for one that knows the Lord, such a person should daily give thanks to God. If not for anything, for the breath of life. Some say that when a child is born, the reason the child cries is because of uncertainty that awaits that child in the world. The child coming from a perfect kingdom into a word filled with troubles usually cries because he or she is worried. Believe it or not, when a child does not cry, the birth attendant and the mother would be concerned. What this simply means is that there is no human being that is not worried about something. It varies from one person to another. Isaiah 30 vs. 19: “For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem: thou shalt weep no more: he will be gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear it, he will answer thee”. God does not want his children to be in a state of tears of pain or sorrow. The Lord detests weeping, he said, “ thou shalt weep no more”. With this, at the back of our minds, we must know that weeping does not glorify God, it solves no problem. If anything, it could endanger one’s health. So what is expected of a Christian is to cry unto the LORD that in God in his grace will hear and answer. Note, the emphasis in the Bible passage quoted. You will first cry to God. Crying is not necessarily about shedding tears but about going to God in prayer. Tears may drop while praying but that is not weeping due to delay or non-manifestation of one’s heart’s desires. The Holy Bible records in the story of Hannah that she was in bitterness of soul. 1st Samuel 1st Samuel 1 vs. 10: “ And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the LORD, and wept sore”. Her tears dropped as she poured out her heart to the God in prayer. In other words, she prayed earnestly. When we pray with total focus on the LORD, the Bible tells us , “he will hear and then answer”. May the LORD hear our prayers as we cry unto Him in Jesus name. Hannah after she prayed and made a vow, continued to wait on the LORD and the Bible records that “ God remembered her”. I may not know what you so desire, as long as it is in line with the word of God, before this month ends, the LORD will remember you in Jesus name. It is written in Isaiah 64 vs. 4: “ For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear , neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee, what he hath prepared for him that waiteth for him”. This Bible passage simply tells us that amazing miracles await those that wait on the Lord. You want to experience a new beginning, then you must be ready to wait patiently in the presence of the God. Brethren, while waiting on the Lord, we must shun provocation and anger as they are tools of the enemy to keep our miracle farther away from us. You don’t believe, let’s see the story of Hannah and Peninnah in 1st Samuel 1 vs. 6: “ And her adversary also provoked her sore, for to make her fret, because the LORD had shut up her womb”. Brethren, if Hannah had given in to Peninnah’s provocation, the house would have become a war zone. Her tears of sorrow would have multiplied because, the children of Peninnah would be on the side of their mother and Hannah would be alone. It would only be a matter of time before Hannah’s husband that loves her switch to the other side. Whatever you are going through right now, the word of God for you is , you are not alone, God is with you in Jesus name. Rather than waste her time fighting and quarrelling, she took her tears to the Lord. Beloved, when last did you have a conversation with the LORD? I mean when last did you create a quite time to thank God for life and remind him that since He created you, you would move from grass to Grace.? It sounds simple but believe me, God responds to such swiftly because, you may not get to that level until you are in Christ and Christ is in you. Provocation and anger are weapons of the enemy to shut the door of God’s mercy against anyone waiting on the Lord. May God give us the Grace to shun these two evils in Jesus name. Apostle Paul told us in 1st Corinthians 16 vs. 9 : ( NIV) “ Because a great door for effective work has opened to me, and there are many who oppose me”. King James Version puts it this way, “ For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and there are many adversaries”. If Penninah knew that God would bless Hannah with a Samuel that would be a man of God and a judge over Israel, she probably would not have provoked her . Peninnah’s provocative attitude led Hannah to make a desperate cry unto the LORD and she got a reward beyond her imagination. That would be someone’s story very soon in Jesus name. The just concluded 74th Annual Convention of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, produced amazing testimonies. I’ll share one to lift up the faith of readers trusting God for one issue or the other. One of the amazing testimonies was that of a woman who said she attended a programme during which our father in the Lord, Daddy Enoch Adejare Adeboye announced that he wanted the Lord to bless his people with 83,000 babies. That should be March last year when he turned 83 . This woman jokingly said, it is the three above the 80 that she would like to have. She must have said this knowing that the blessing that our Daddy G.O. requested isn’t for her alone. The most important point in her testimony that many of us missed, is that what she had was a conversation with the LORD which she counted as a joke. Unknown to her, anyone that has a strong relationship with the LORD cannot utter words jokingly because her thoughts and words are anointed and God would honour such words. While giving her testimony, she had with her a set of triplets. Beloved, be determined to move from tears to laughter . Someone in a conversation with the Lord, may appear abnormal to others because, the person is not praying like Hannah on the altar of God but a person that has a conversation with God is a person has total trust in God and has become a friend of Jesus. Are you his friend already? If not, begin to take steps to improve your relationship with Christ. It isn’t too late. Brethren, be prepared for the September Holy Ghost night. It is a programme for people trusting God for children and other things. Be there, it is your turn to laugh. It is well. The post From tears to laughter, by Funmi Komolafe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Security man martyred in Mastung attack
items.description: QUETTA: A security official embraced martyrdom and six others sustained injuries in a roadside bomb explosion in the Khad Kocha area of Mastung district on Saturday, police said. Officials said that an explosive device planted in the Gro area of Khad Kocha along the Quetta-Karachi National Highway was detonated when security vehicles were passing through the area. One of the vehicles was hit in the blast, resulting in the martyrdom of a security official and injuring six others, a senior police officer confirmed to Dawn , adding that other vehicles remain safe in the blast. After the explosion, a heavy exchange of fire continued for some time. “Miscreants escaped from the site as soon as more security personnel rea­ched the area,” police officials said. In the meantime, the body and the injured were rushed to the Nawab Ghous Bakhsh Raisani Memorial Hospital. The highway was closed following the blast that suspended all traffic at various points, while a search operation was launched in the area to trace the miscreants. Just a day ago, four labourers working in an apple orchard were killed and three others injured in an explosion in the same area. Hospital officials who examined the bodies and the injured noted visible splinter marks on them. Published in Dawn, August 23rd, 2026

items.title: JoyNews-Republic Bank Habitat Fair 2026: Today’s finale offers final chance to turn housing dreams into reality
items.description: The final day of the JoyNews-Republic Bank Habitat Fair 2026 mini-fair comes up today, Sunday, August 23, with organisers expecting a strong turnout as the three-day housing and construction showcase enters its closing stretch at the Achimota Retail Centre. After two days of steady patronage, lively engagements and expert interactions, the fair is set for its final push, offering prospective homeowners, property investors, builders and families one last opportunity to explore products, services and solutions designed to make home ownership more achievable. Held under the theme “Dream it. Explore it. Own it,” the fair has provided a meeting point for people at different stages of the housing journey, from those only beginning to explore their options to patrons actively looking for financing, building materials, property and home improvement solutions. Final chance to explore The closing day is expected to attract patrons who may have been unable to attend earlier or who want more time to engage exhibitors, compare options and seek professional advice before making decisions. Exhibitors across the housing ecosystem will continue to showcase solutions covering building materials, home financing, construction, furnishing, property development and related services, giving visitors an opportunity to have direct conversations with businesses and industry professionals. For prospective homeowners, the final day presents an opportunity to move beyond simply dreaming about a home and begin identifying the practical steps, products and financial options required to make that dream a reality. The first two days have seen prospective homeowners, builders, industry professionals and other visitors interact with exhibitors despite intermittent drizzle in Accra on Saturday. The weather did little to slow activity at the fairgrounds, where patrons moved between exhibition stands, sought advice and explored alternatives suited to their housing needs. The fair is designed to bridge the gap between aspiration and action by bringing key players in the housing and construction sector together in one location. For many visitors, the event has offered more than a conventional exhibition. It has provided an opportunity to ask questions, obtain practical guidance, compare products and better understand the processes involved in building, buying, financing or improving a home. Sunday finale With the final day now here, organisers are encouraging members of the public to take advantage of the remaining opportunity to engage exhibitors and professionals. The mini-fair is being organised in partnership with Republic Bank, under its brand promise, “We’re the one for you!”, and powered by Drive EV GH, which promotes sustainable mobility. Other partners supporting the initiative are Virtual Security Africa, Akwaaba Building Materials, Lesh Fortune Ltd, MTN, Door Masters, Ayuda, Western Vilas, CTECHI Ghana LTD, Saint-Gobain Ghana, Sintex Tank, Interplast and Clifton Homes. The collaboration brings together businesses and service providers from across the housing value chain, strengthening the fair’s role as a platform for connecting consumers with solutions for their housing ambitions. As the three-day event prepares to draw the curtain, today’s climax is expected to provide one final opportunity for patrons to discover what is available in Ghana’s housing and construction market. For those who have been considering building, buying, financing or improving a home, the organisers’ invitation is straightforward for you to make Sunday count. The fair continues today at the Achimota Retail Centre, giving patrons a final opportunity to explore the possibilities, engage the experts and take a step closer to turning their housing aspirations into reality.

items.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: REVOLUTION TO NOWHERE?
items.description: In 2007, the so-called ‘Lawyers’ Movement’ in Pakistan mobilised immense pressure against then military ruler Gen Pervez Musharraf to reinstate Chief Justice Iftikhar Chaudhry, whom Musharraf had arbitrarily dismissed. Backed by opposition parties, these protests catalysed a somewhat ‘fair’ 2008 general election, which brought the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) to power, closely followed by the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N). Leveraging their combined parliamentary majority, the two major parties threatened impeachment unless Musharraf relinquished power and retired. He complied, signalling a victory for the protest movement. However, this success was short-lived. What followed was the reinstatement of a judge who began to practice overt judicial populism and hound the fragile PPP ruling coalition, alongside a military establishment led by Gen Pervez Kayani. In fact, some political commentators have suggested that Kayani had quietly allowed the Lawyers’ Movement to mushroom as a way to force Musharraf to hand over the post of army chief to him. The PPP coalition faced severe judicial populism from Chaudhry, constant bullying from Kayani’s military establishment, unprecedented terror attacks from Islamist militants and an opposition that jumped on these bandwagons. It was a chaotic period. This episode illustrates a classic example of how ‘horizontal movements’ are capable of removing a powerful political figure and even a government, yet almost always fail to produce structural change. Musharraf’s fall actually worsened matters because the problematic political and economic structures not only remained intact but deepened. Decentralised movements can mobilise millions without a central command, but their greatest strength can also become their greatest weakness. Once the common enemy disappears, what holds the movement together? Horizontal movements are decentralised forms of social and political activism that operate without a traditional hierarchical leadership. Unlike top-down organisations with a central command system, horizontal movements rely on spontaneous mobilisation, peer-to-peer collaboration and consensus-based decision-making. These movements often bring together diverse groups, ranging from professional associations and student outfits to ordinary citizens and opposition parties, united by a common grievance against an authority figure or regime. Their lack of a single leader makes them difficult to suppress, as there is no single figurehead to arrest or negotiate with. But according to the American sociologists F. Fox Piven and Richard Cloward, while horizontal movements can become effective catalysts for challenging authority and dismantling regimes, their decentralised nature introduces several disadvantages. These vulnerabilities often explain why such movements succeed in disruption but fail in reconstruction. In 2017, the political theorists Michael Hardt and Antonio Negri wrote that horizontal movements suffer from a lack of unified vision. Due to the fact that participants unite against a common grievance rather than a shared ideology, internal cracks quickly emerge once the shared enemy is removed, leaving groups deeply divided on how to govern. Such movements lack institutional depth. Mainstream political parties have chains of command and administrative experience, whereas horizontal movements struggle to transition from street-level protest to sustainable governance. This vacuum is often exploited by entrenched state institutions and governments. Yet, ever since the 1990s, horizontal movements have overtaken the concept of ‘vertical movements’ that rely on hierarchies, central party leadership and top-down command structures to effect social and political change. Historically, vertical movements have a better record of enforcing structural changes. Some general examples in this regard include anti-colonial independence struggles led by disciplined party structures and organised labour movements backed by union hierarchies. These demonstrated a much stronger capacity to build institutional machinery, seize state power and enforce lasting structural and legal changes.. Illustration by Abro Most political scientists posit that vertical movements have largely fallen out of favour due to a widespread disillusionment with traditional political parties, governments and labour unions, making people deeply sceptical of top-down leadership. The Spanish sociologist Manuel Castells believes that the rise of the internet, social media and encrypted communication platforms enables swift, decentralised coordination without requiring a central committee or formal organisation. Recent research suggests that horizontal structures are valued for being faster to form and more welcoming to diverse groups, as participants do not need to submit to party discipline or ideological doctrines. The barrier to participation is lower, making it much easier for individuals to join a spontaneous, decentralised protest or online campaign than to commit to the long-term, disciplined membership required by traditional vertical structures. Over the past two decades, nearly all major uprisings have been organised along horizontal lines. On the surface, these movements are frequently deemed successful and their impact receives sensationalist coverage in both mainstream and social media. Yet, the failure of horizontally organised movements to enact structural change is rarely scrutinised. While these movements have succeeded in removing unpopular leaders and, in some cases, entire governments, these victories merely create vacuums that are swiftly filled by entrenched powers, particularly when these powers successfully replicate and co-opt the tenor, slogans and even participants of the original movements. The Arab Spring uprisings are a case in point. Across several countries in the Middle East and North Africa, decentralised horizontal networks successfully toppled long-standing authoritarian rulers, such as in Tunisia and Egypt. However, because these movements lacked well-thought-out alternatives, apart from abstract demands and slogans, the ensuing political vacuums were initially filled by organised Islamist groups and then by entrenched military institutions that co-opted the rhetoric of the uprisings. In the United States, the left-leaning ‘Occupy Wall Street’ movement captured global attention and mainstream media coverage regarding economic inequality following the 2008 financial crisis. According to the American political scientist John Ehrenberg, since the movement was horizontal, it struggled to translate street-level momentum into lasting legislative policy, leaving existing financial and political structures entirely intact, while mainstream political parties later absorbed parts of its populist rhetoric for electoral campaigns. In the early 2010s, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in India and the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) in Pakistan also did exactly that. In developing countries, the expansion of the middle class is another factor that has popularised the growth of horizontal movements. Rising educational attainment, urbanisation and access to digital technology have created a population with higher expectations for governance, transparency and personal autonomy. Unlike traditional working-class movements tied to union hierarchies or rural-agrarian networks, this growing urban middle class in developing countries often feels alienated by supposedly fossilised political parties and state institutions. They prefer flexible, decentralised networks that reflect their modern interconnected lifestyles and allow them to mobilise around specific grievances without submitting to traditional party discipline. Their initiatives in this regard are as much political endeavours as they are performative and aesthetic. While these movements can, and often do, succeed in removing ministers and governments, when their participants are basking in the glow of victory, entrenched state institutions are often already filling the vacuum left unaddressed by horizontal movements. Structural and sustained institutional reconstruction demands a lot more energy and (offline) effort. Middle-class horizontal movements seem to be hesitant in this regard. Perhaps because the overarching desire is to become a part of the entrenched elites in the future? Published in Dawn, EOS, August 23rd, 2026

items.title: Kagbelen Village : un train de RUSAL déraille et percute un tricycle
items.description: Un accident ferroviaire s’est produit dans la soirée de ce samedi 22 août 2026 à Kagbelen Village, dans la commune de Kagbelen. Un train de la compagnie RUSAL, transportant de la bauxite, a déraillé avant de percuter un tricycle qui transportait six passagers. Plusieurs blessés ont été enregistrés. Selon un témoin présent sur les lieux, le train roulait à vive allure lorsqu’un des wagons s’est détaché. La locomotive a ensuite quitté les rails et s’est retrouvée à quelques mètres de la chaussée, avant de percuter le tricycle. « L’accident s’est produit dans la soirée, ici à Kagbelen Village. Le train roulait à vive allure quand, tout à coup, l’un des wagons s’est détaché et la locomotive a quitté les rails pour se retrouver à quelques mètres de l’asphalte. Elle a alors percuté un tricycle qui transportait six passagers. Sous l’impact et sous le poids de la bauxite transportée, le tricycle a été projeté, blessant ses occupants. L’un d’eux a été grièvement touché ; il a fallu découper son pantalon pour lui porter secours », rapporte le témoin. Alerté, le premier vice-maire de Kagbelen s’est rendu sur les lieux pour constater la situation. « J’ai été alerté par le chef du quartier de Kagbelen Village qu’un train de RUSAL avait déraillé et s’était immobilisé au bord de la route. Heureusement, aucune perte en vie humaine n’est à déplorer, mais quatre wagons restent bloqués », a-t-il déclaré. Au moment de la mise en ligne de cette dépêche, les forces de défense et de sécurité étaient déployées sur les lieux afin de sécuriser la zone et de faciliter la circulation. Mayi CISSÉ L’article Kagbelen Village : un train de RUSAL déraille et percute un tricycle est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Mondial 2030 : L’Espagne relance son offensive pour accueillir la finale
items.description: La bataille d’influence autour de la finale de la Coupe du monde 2030 se poursuit. Alors que la FIFA n’a toujours pas désigné le stade qui accueillera l’ultime rencontre du tournoi organisé conjointement par le Maroc, l’Espagne et le Portugal, le président de la Fédération espagnole de football (RFEF), Rafael Louzán, a relancé publiquement la candidature de son pays, mettant encore plus la pression sur la FIFA. Dans des déclarations radiophoniques, le dirigeant espagnol a estimé qu’« il serait incompréhensible que la finale de la Coupe du monde ne se dispute pas en Espagne », une position qu’il justifie par « la place du pays dans le paysage footballistique international » ainsi que par la qualité de ses infrastructures sportives. Rafael Louzán a par ailleurs affiché sa confiance dans la réussite de l’édition 2030, saluant la coopération entre l’Espagne, le Maroc et le Portugal. Selon lui, les capacités des trois pays à accueillir de grands événements sportifs constituent un atout majeur pour faire de cette Coupe du monde une édition de référence. Ces prises de position s’inscrivent dans une stratégie de communication récurrente de la part des responsables espagnols, qui multiplient les interventions publiques afin de convaincre la FIFA de confier à l’Espagne l’organisation de la finale. Face à cette offensive, le Maroc continue lui aussi de défendre sa candidature, une ambition réaffirmée à plusieurs reprises par les responsables du football national. Deux enceintes cristallisent aujourd’hui les ambitions des deux pays. L’Espagne souhaite voir le Santiago-Bernabéu, à Madrid, accueillir le match le plus attendu du tournoi. De son côté, le Maroc mise sur le futur stade Hassan II de Benslimane, près de Casablanca, actuellement en chantier et appelé à devenir l’un des symboles majeurs du Mondial 2030. L’enceinte marocaine devrait disposer d’une capacité d’environ 115.000 places. Une fois achevée, elle deviendrait le plus grand stade au monde en matière d’accueil de spectateurs, un argument de poids dans la compétition qui l’oppose aux candidatures espagnoles pour l’organisation de la finale. Au-delà de la question du match décisif, plusieurs inconnues demeurent. La FIFA n’a pas encore arrêté la répartition définitive des rencontres entre les trois pays hôtes. Si l’Espagne et le Maroc devraient accueillir la majorité des matches, le Portugal devrait disposer d’un nombre plus limité de rencontres. Dans ce contexte, le contraste est notable entre les approches adoptées par les deux principaux prétendants à la finale. Tandis que la Fédération espagnole assume une campagne publique en faveur de sa candidature, la partie marocaine privilégie jusqu’à présent une démarche plus institutionnelle, s’appuyant sur les procédures de la FIFA et sur le travail diplomatique mené par la Fédération royale marocaine de football et son président, Fouzi Lekjaa. Le dossier reste donc ouvert et devrait continuer d’alimenter les débats au cours des prochaines années. En attendant la décision de la FIFA, le Maroc poursuit la préparation de ses infrastructures. Le Royaume devrait disposer de six à sept stades pour le Mondial 2030, répartis notamment entre Rabat, Benslimane, Tanger, Marrakech et Agadir, confirmant l’ampleur du dispositif prévu pour accueillir l’événement planétaire. items.title: Mahama pushes for five permanent UN Security Council seats for Africa
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has proposed a major restructuring of the United Nations Security Council to give Africa five permanent seats, saying the arrangement would provide the continent with a fairer voice in decisions on global peace and security. Under the proposal, each of Africa’s five geographical regions would have a permanent representative on the Council, giving the continent a collective presence that reflects its regional diversity. President Mahama made the proposal in an exclusive interview with TRT World in which he advocated reforms to the UN system and urged African countries to develop a common position on the restructuring of the Security Council. He said allocating five permanent seats to Africa would be a more appropriate arrangement than granting the continent only one or two positions. “I think it would have been best if we got five seats, because Africa has five regions. And so each region would have representation,” he said. President Mahama, however, cautioned against combining the demand for additional permanent seats with an immediate push to reform the veto powers enjoyed by the current permanent members of the Security Council. He argued that Africa’s immediate priority should be to build broad international support for an expanded Council and secure better representation before opening negotiations on the more contentious question of veto rights. In his view, attempting to resolve both issues simultaneously could complicate negotiations with the existing permanent members. “We need a two-step solution. And so we should speak with one voice and ask for an expansion of the Security Council. Once we expand the Security Council and we have better representation of the Security Council, then we can discuss the veto,” he said. The President said a united African position would be critical to advancing the continent’s interests in any negotiations on UN reform. He maintained that African countries could work towards an agreement on which states should represent the continent if the proposal for five permanent seats gains international backing. The call comes amid longstanding concerns over what many African leaders regard as the continent’s inadequate representation in the UN’s highest decision-making body, despite Africa’s significant role in the organisation’s peace and security agenda. President Mahama’s proposal would, therefore, shift the debate from whether Africa should have a permanent presence on the Security Council to how broad and representative that presence should be .

items.title: Ouagadougou : La dégradation de la route Tanghin-Tampouy inquiète les usagers
items.description: À Ouagadougou, la route reliant l'hôpital Schifra au début de l'échangeur de Tampouy se trouve aujourd'hui dans un état de dégradation avancée. Nids-de-poule, gros trous, chaussée étroite et absence d'éclairage public rendent la circulation particulièrement difficile, surtout aux heures de pointe et la nuit. Les usagers appellent à une réhabilitation urgente de cette voie très fréquentée. La route Tanghin-Tampouy est devenue un véritable parcours d'obstacles pour les usagers. Sur plusieurs portions, les nids-de-poule et les gros trous ont considérablement dégradé la chaussée. À cela s'ajoute l'étroitesse de la voie, qui complique davantage la circulation lorsque le trafic devient important. Chaque matin, à partir de 7 heures, et en fin de journée, dès 16 heures, la circulation s'intensifie sur cet axe qui permet de relier plusieurs quartiers de la capitale, notamment Tampouy, Tanghin et Somgandé. Mais l'état de la chaussée expose quotidiennement les conducteurs, notamment les motocyclistes, à des chutes et à des accidents. Pour certains usagers, emprunter cette route est devenu une source d'inquiétude. Erwan Compaoré raconte avoir lui-même été victime d'une chute sur cet axe. « L'état de la voie de Tanghin-Tampouy est piteux. J'ai arrêté d'emprunter cette voie parce qu'un soir, je quittais Tampouy pour me rendre à la maison à Bendogo. Je roulais et, le temps que je me rende compte, j'étais à terre en train d'observer les étoiles. J'ai compris que je venais de faire une chute », témoigne-t-il. Selon lui, les accidents et les chutes sont devenus presque habituels sur cette route. « Bizarrement, lorsque vous tombez sur cette route, c'est comme si c'était devenu la règle normale », déplore-t-il. Erwan Compaoré rapporte également les propos d'un homme venu lui porter secours après sa chute. « Ce dernier m'a dit que cette voie est dangereuse : aujourd'hui, c'est toi ; hier, c'était un enfant ; avant-hier, c'était une vieille personne », raconte-t-il. Une autre partie de la voie De son côté, Moumouni Kaboré, qui emprunte régulièrement cet axe, déplore également l'état de la chaussée. « Cette route devient de plus en plus impraticable. À la moindre erreur, tu te retrouves à terre. Et les motos subissent beaucoup de chocs », affirme-t-il. Habitant à Tampouy et travaillant à Dassasgho, il explique emprunter cette route presque quotidiennement. « Je vous assure que chaque matin et chaque soir, je suis angoissé à l'idée de prendre cette voie. C'est une véritable source de stress pour moi », confie-t-il. Selon lui, les nombreuses secousses ont également des conséquences sur l'état de sa moto. « Chaque fois, ma moto tombe en panne à cause des secousses », ajoute-t-il. Outre les dégradations de la chaussée, l'étroitesse de la voie constitue une autre difficulté. Lorsque plusieurs usagers se retrouvent simultanément sur l'axe, les possibilités d'évitement deviennent limitées. Un conducteur peut facilement se retrouver en dehors de la chaussée pour éviter un autre usager ou un nid-de-poule, avec le risque de perdre le contrôle de son engin. Une partie de la voie dégradée Pour Adji Ouédraogo, la situation est devenue tellement difficile qu'elle évite désormais cette route, sauf en cas de nécessité. « C'est pour une urgence que j'emprunte cette route. Elle devient un calvaire pour nous, les usagers de cette route », estime-t-elle. Elle dénonce notamment la présence de nombreux trous qui rendent la circulation dangereuse. « À la moindre erreur, tu te retrouves dans un trou. Il faut que les autorités nous viennent en aide, sinon ce n'est pas simple », lance-t-elle. La situation devient encore plus préoccupante à la tombée de la nuit. L'absence d'éclairage sur cette portion réduit considérablement la visibilité et augmente les risques d'accident. Pour les personnes qui découvrent cette route, la circulation nocturne peut ainsi devenir particulièrement dangereuse. Au-delà des difficultés rencontrées par les usagers, cette voie joue pourtant un rôle important dans la mobilité urbaine. Elle constitue un axe de liaison pour de nombreux habitants. Face à cette situation, les usagers appellent les autorités compétentes à prendre des mesures pour réhabiliter la route, améliorer son éclairage et renforcer la sécurité de la circulation. Pour eux, une intervention rapide permettrait non seulement de réduire les risques d'accident, mais aussi d'améliorer la mobilité dans cette partie de la capitale. Rama Diallo Lefaso.net

items.title: See areas to be affected by GRIDCo’s planned 15-hour power outage today
items.description: Several communities and businesses in the Greater Accra Region are expected to experience a prolonged power interruption today, Sunday, August 23, 2026, as the Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo) undertakes critical work to replace a transmission tower damaged in a tanker explosion. The planned outage, which will last 15 hours, is scheduled to run from 3 a.m. to 6 p.m. and will affect customers within parts of the Accra West and Accra East operational areas of the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG). GRIDCo said the shutdown was necessary to enable its engineers and technical teams to safely complete work on the damaged structure and restore the affected transmission line. The tower forms part of the 161kV Tema-Achimota transmission line at the Ashaiman section. The exercise is expected to affect a wide range of residential communities, commercial centres and business districts across the capital, with ECG advising customers within the affected areas to make the necessary arrangements ahead of the interruption. Communities to be affected In the Accra West operational area, the affected locations include James Town, Mamprobi, Chorkor, Sempe, parts of Kaneshie, North Industrial Area, Okaishie, Agbogbloshie, Kantamanto, Adabraka and parts of Ridge. Other areas listed are Tesano, Santana Market, parts of Alajo, Malam Atta Market, Asylum Down and surrounding communities. Customers in the Accra East operational area who are expected to experience the outage include residents and businesses in Nima Township, Kanda Highway, Kanda Estate, Kokomlemle, Sulana, Circle, Madina Township, Okponglo, Cantonment and Osu Oxford Street. The interruption will also affect surrounding communities within the operational areas. Safety concerns GRIDCo said the planned shutdown was essential to provide a safe working environment for the teams carrying out the tower replacement. The company is collaborating with ECG to complete the work and restore power to affected customers as quickly as possible. The damaged tower is understood to have compromised an important section of the transmission network, making its replacement necessary to ensure the continued reliability and safety of the electricity supply system. GRIDCo apologised to customers and businesses for the inconvenience the exercise would cause and appealed for their patience and understanding. The company said the work was being undertaken as part of efforts to restore the integrity of the transmission infrastructure and ensure reliable power supply to customers. Residents and businesses in the affected communities have consequently been urged to plan for the extended interruption and take appropriate measures to minimise its impact.

Sergio Alegre, Óscar Hernández, Ruud van Nistelrooy et Adil Ramzi rejoindront l'équipe en tant qu’entraîneurs adjoints”, a indiqué la fédération sur son site web. Patrick Lodewijks revient en tant qu'entraîneur des gardiens de but, tandis qu'Iván Torres complète le staff en tant qu'entraîneur de performance, a ajouté la même source. Adil Ramzi intègre l’équipe de Xavi Hernandez après avoir pris les rênes de la sélection néerlandaise des U18 en 2024 puis de celle des U19 un an plus tard, a rappelé la fédération, notant qu’avant cela, l’ancien Lion de l’Atlas a travaillé au PSV Eindhoven, entre autres, en tant qu'entraîneur adjoint de l'équipe première et coach principal de l’équipe réserve (Jong PSV). En tant que joueur, Ramzi a porté notamment les couleurs des clubs néerlandais du PSV, de l'AZ Alkmaar et du FC Twente. Il compte également 37 sélections pour le Maroc. La KNVB avait nommé la semaine dernière l'entraîneur espagnol Xavi Hernandez au poste de sélectionneur des Oranje. items.title: Debutant Espi gives Mourinho a winning Real Madrid return
items.description: Jose Mourinho’s first competitive match of his second spell as Real Madrid manager ended with a thrilling 90th-minute winner from his side at Espanyol. The visitors took the lead in the ninth minute when England midfielder Jude Bellingham headed in Arda Guler’s wide free-kick. But Espanyol levelled in the 30th minute through summer signing Cala, who tapped in Javi Hernandez’s cut-back at the far post. Real dominated for much of the encounter and twice hit the woodwork before their dramatic late winner from debutant Carlos Espi. Bellingham had another powerful header tipped on to the bar by Espanyol keeper Marko Dmitrovic, while Federico Valverde’s curling effort hit the base of the post. But the Spanish giants brought on talent from the bench to change the outcome, including summer signings Espi, Marc Cucurella, Yan Diomande – Real’s record signing from RB Leipzig in a deal worth up to £120m – and England full-back Trent Alexander-Arnold. Espi, who joined from Levante for £21m, struck after Diomande had found Kylian Mbappe in the box and the ball fell invitingly for the Spanish forward to calmly finish. After being frustrated by his side’s inability to break down the hosts, the victory delighted Mourinho, who was named Real manager on a three-year deal in July, and started new signings Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konate and Bernardo Silva. His previous spell began in 2010 and lasted three seasons, yielding a La Liga title, the Copa del Rey and Spanish Super Cup. The 63-year-old Mourinho has won 26 major official trophies across his managerial career, including three Premier League titles with Chelsea and Champions League titles at both Porto and Inter Milan. Real have failed to win a trophy in their past two seasons and parted ways with Xabi Alonso in January, before Alvaro Arbeloa led them through to the end of the campaign in a temporary spell.

items.title: 2027 Budget Statement must pivot around job creation, greater transparency – CSOs to government
items.description: Civil society organisations (CSOs) have called on the government to make job creation, stronger revenue mobilisation and greater transparency central to the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy. They also want the government to strengthen the management of mineral revenues, close tax loopholes, tackle illicit financial flows and ensure that Ghana derives measurable benefits from tax exemptions granted to companies. The demands were made at a CSO engagement on the 2027 Budget in Accra, where representatives of the Economic Governance Platform, the National Resource Governance Institute (NRGI), the Africa Centre for Energy Policy (ACEP) and the Tax Justice Coalition presented proposals for consideration by the Ministry of Finance. The forum, organised by the Economic Governance Platform and Oxfam, was aimed at gathering inputs from civil society into the 2027 Budget and the medium-term framework. The engagement comes as the government prepares the 2027 Budget, which Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson is expected to present to Parliament in November. The minister has previously indicated that the government’s proposed “New Economy” programme, aimed at moving the economy from stability to accelerated development and job creation, will be outlined in the 2027 Budget. From stability to jobs On the macroeconomic outlook, a representative of the Economic Governance Platform, Ebenezer Okley, said the government should leverage the gains made in macroeconomic stability to deliver concrete benefits to Ghanaians. He said while the government had focused significantly on restoring macroeconomic stability over the past year and into 2026, the priority for the 2027 Budget should be to translate that stability into jobs, price stability and improved welfare. He said the 2027 Budget should clearly demonstrate how macroeconomic stability would lead to increased employment and stronger economic fundamentals. Mineral revenue On the extractive sector, David Adjei of NRGI called for a comprehensive framework for managing mineral revenues. He said mineral revenues were currently governed by different laws and proposed that royalties, taxes and other mineral-related revenues be brought under a single framework to make it easier to track how the proceeds were collected, allocated and spent. Under the proposed framework, he said, mineral revenues could be channelled into the national budget, savings for future generations and sub-national governments. Mr Adjei also called for greater clarity on the mandate and financing of the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF), questioning whether its current allocation of two per cent of mineral royalties was sufficient to enable the fund to effectively manage mineral-related investments. Mr Adjei further called for clearer boundaries around the expanding functions of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) to prevent overlaps with institutions such as the Minerals Commission and other state agencies. He also raised concerns about the limited disclosure surrounding the reported acquisition of the Ewoyaa lithium project, owned by Atlantic Lithium, by a Chinese company. He called on the government to ensure transparency in such transactions by disclosing the beneficial ownership, transaction terms and valuation benchmarks associated with the transfer of critical mineral assets. The speakers and the participants in the CSOs forum on the 2027 Budget Small-scale mining The NRGI representative also called for measures to increase the fiscal contribution of the artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) sector. He said despite the boom in gold exports and rising mineral royalties, the contribution of the ASM sector remained low. He advocated the formalisation of ASM operations and the introduction of measures to ensure that operators contributed appropriately to government revenue. Tax compliance, incentives For the Tax Justice Coalition, its National Coordinator, Benedict Doh, called for stronger action against illicit financial flows and greater transparency in the granting of tax exemptions. He said literature indicated that about 65 per cent of illicit financial flows were associated with commercial activities, making stronger transfer-pricing enforcement critical to protecting domestic revenue. Mr Doh also proposed incentives to encourage voluntary tax compliance. He suggested that taxpayers who insisted on receiving VAT invoices or receipts from businesses could be rewarded through tax reliefs, refunds or other incentives. He said such a system could encourage consumers to demand VAT invoices and thereby help businesses to accurately account for their tax obligations. Mr Doh said Ghana’s tax-to-GDP ratio, currently at about 13 per cent, remained below the government’s medium-term target of 18 per cent by the end of 2027.

items.title: La démission de Bouaïda ébranle l'Istiqlal et sa prochaine destination politique reste inconnue
items.description: Le député parlementaire Abderrahim Bouaïda a officiellement annoncé sa démission du Parti de l’Istiqlal, justifiant sa décision par le fait qu’il n’a pas été retenu parmi les candidats investis par le parti. Dans une vidéo publiée sur sa page personnelle Facebook, Bouaïda s’est interrogé sur le critère politique sur lequel le parti s’est fondé pour investir une autre personne à sa place. Il a notamment souligné que la personne choisie dans la circonscription où il s’était porté candidat faisait, au cours de la précédente législature, l’objet de poursuites judiciaires. Tout en exprimant son respect pour le Parti de l’Istiqlal et pour ses militants, avec lesquels il a passé de nombreuses années, il n’a, en revanche, pas caché que sa démission constituait pour lui une décision irrévocable. Il l’a expliquée par son désaccord avec les promesses qui lui avaient été faites et par son refus de se montrer « opportuniste » , selon ses propres termes, en réduisant la politique à un poste, à une investiture ou à des calculs électoraux. Il a, à cette occasion, réaffirmé son attachement à ses convictions. Bouaïda a poursuivi : « Si vous considérez que, en tant que député du Parti de l’Istiqlal, je n’ai pas respecté la Charte de la majorité et que, depuis mon positionnement au sein d’un parti participant au gouvernement, je critiquais la politique gouvernementale, alors j’accepte que cela fasse de moi une personne indésirable. » Le député de la circonscription de Guelmim a poursuivi avec fermeté : « Je ne démissionnerai pas de mes positions pour obtenir une investiture » , soulignant que, même s’il quitte le Parti de l’Istiqlal, cela ne signifie pas pour autant qu’il se détourne de la politique ni de la « défense des citoyens ». Abderrahim Bouaïda a conclu qu’un homme politique qui se tait uniquement pour préserver son investiture peut certes rester candidat au sein du parti, mais qu’à ses yeux, il restera dépourvu de positions. Il a insisté sur le fait que, personnellement, il préfère perdre l’investiture plutôt que de perdre « lui-même et ses positions ». Il a ajouté que cette démission représente pour lui « autant la fin d’une étape qu’elle ouvre la voie à une nouvelle », soulevant ainsi la question de la prochaine destination politique de Bouaïda après la fin de son parcours avec le Parti de l’Istiqlal. The post La démission de Bouaïda ébranle l'Istiqlal et sa prochaine destination politique reste inconnue appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

La HAC prévient également qu’en cas de récidive ou de non-exécution de cette mesure, elle pourra prononcer des sanctions immédiates, pouvant aller jusqu’à la suspension temporaire des programmes de Télé 24. items.title: Debt servicing now below 20% of revenue — Ato Forson
items.description: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana has significantly reduced the share of national revenue devoted to servicing public debt, with the figure now falling below 20 per cent. He said the development represented a major shift from the country’s previous debt-service burden, when more than half of national revenue was used to meet debt obligations. Dr Ato Forson made the disclosure in a Facebook post on Saturday, August 22, 2026, highlighting what he described as progress in Ghana’s efforts to restore fiscal stability. “In the past, Ghana spent over 50 percent of its national revenue on servicing debt,” he posted. According to the Minister, the high debt-service burden in the past severely constrained the resources available to finance critical public services and infrastructure. “This left less money for schools, hospitals, roads and other essential infrastructure,” he added. He said the reduction in the proportion of revenue allocated to debt servicing had created greater fiscal space for government to pursue its development priorities. From over 50% to below 20% Dr Ato Forson said the latest position marked significant progress compared with the situation in which more than 50 per cent of government revenue was absorbed by debt servicing. “Today, I am proud to say that we have made significant progress. We now spend less than 20 percent of our revenue on servicing debt!” The Minister’s comments highlight the importance of debt sustainability to the government’s broader fiscal consolidation agenda, particularly in an economy where debt-service obligations have historically competed with expenditure on social services and infrastructure. A reduction in the share of revenue devoted to debt servicing means a larger proportion of government’s internally generated resources can potentially be directed towards priority areas, although the actual fiscal space available will also depend on revenue performance, expenditure pressures and other government obligations. Dr Ato Forson’s statement comes as the government continues to emphasise fiscal discipline, debt restructuring and measures aimed at restoring confidence in Ghana’s public finances.

items.title: Urgent / Medias : la HAC met « en demeure » la chaîne Télé24 après la diffusion d’un reportage sur un ministre limogé
items.description: La décision vient de tomber. La Haute Autorité de la Communication (HAC) a mis en demeure la chaîne de télévision privée « Télé 24 » à la suite de la diffusion, dans son journal télévisé de 20 heures du samedi 22 août 2026, d’un reportage consacré à une cérémonie officielle présidée par un ministre limogé la veille par décret présidentiel. La décision, référencée N°030/HAC/P/2026 et signée à Conakry le 22 août 2026 dont Guineenews a reçu copie, intervient à l’issue d’une séance extraordinaire de l’institution tenue le même jour. Elle fait suite au rapport de monitoring des médias de la HAC portant sur le journal télévisé de la chaîne. Selon le document, la chaîne privée a diffusé « au cours de son journal télévisé de 20 heures du samedi 22 août 2026, le reportage d’une cérémonie officielle présidée par un ministre limogé la veille par décret du Président de la République », indique la décision signée par le président de la HAC Boubacar Yacine Diallo. Pour la HAC, cette diffusion constitue un manquement aux obligations professionnelles qui s’imposent aux médias. L’institution estime que la présentation du ministre comme étant toujours en fonction pouvait induire le public en erreur. « Considérant que la diffusion d’une telle information, présentant un ministre limogé comme étant toujours en fonction, constitue un manquement grave aux obligations de vérification des faits, de rigueur professionnelle et de responsabilité sociale qui incombent aux professionnels de la presse », souligne la décision. La Haute Autorité de la Communication ajoute que « la diffusion d’un tel contenu est de nature à induire le public en erreur » . Le reportage doit être retiré de tous les canaux Dans sa décision, la HAC ordonne à la direction générale de Télé 24 de retirer le reportage concerné de l’ensemble de ses supports de diffusion, dès notification de la mise en demeure. L’article 2 de la décision précise ainsi : « Il est ordonné à la Direction générale de la chaîne « Télé 24 » de procéder au retrait, sur l’ensemble de ses canaux de diffusion, du reportage impliquant le ministre limogé, dès notification de la présente décision. » La HAC présente cette mesure comme un avertissement solennel adressé à la chaîne. Elle prévient toutefois que tout manquement ultérieur pourrait entraîner des mesures plus sévères. « La présente mise en demeure constitue un avertissement solennel. En cas de récidive ou de non-exécution des obligations mentionnées à l’article 2, la HAC prononcera des sanctions immédiates pouvant aller jusqu’à la suspension temporaire des programmes de la chaîne » , avertit l’institution. La décision signée par le président de lorgane de régulation des medias en Guinée, Boubacar Yacine Diallo, prend effet à compter de sa date de signature et doit également être enregistrée et publiée au Journal officiel de la République. La mesure intervient alors que la HAC rappelle, dans les visas de sa décision, son fondement juridique, notamment la Loi organique relative à la liberté de la presse ainsi que celle portant attributions, composition, organisation et fonctionnement de la Haute Autorité de la Communication. Ainsi, au-delà du retrait du reportage incriminé, la HAC adresse un rappel aux médias sur la nécessité de vérifier les informations avant leur diffusion, particulièrement lorsqu’elles concernent des changements intervenus au sommet de l’administration publique.

items.title: Chamber of Mines backs government’s Adamus revival plan
items.description: The Ghana Chamber of Mines has commended the Government for what it describes as a major step towards resolving the longstanding impasse involving Adamus Resources Limited, describing the development as a positive signal for investor confidence and the future of indigenous mining in the country. In a statement issued in Accra on August 21, 2026, the Chamber welcomed the decision by stakeholders to implement a 12-month roadmap aimed at restoring the operations of the mining company through a six-member joint management team. According to the Chamber, the arrangement reflects a commitment to dialogue and collaboration while helping to preserve a productive mining asset that remains important to Ghana’s economy. The Chamber noted that Adamus Resources occupies a strategic position within Ghana’s mining landscape as one of the country’s few indigenous large-scale mining operations. It said the successful revival of the mine would help protect jobs, sustain local businesses and support host communities while safeguarding the company’s contribution to government revenue and the broader mining value chain. Commendation for government The industry body particularly praised the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources and the leadership of the Minerals Commission for what it described as their efforts in securing a practical resolution to the dispute. It also acknowledged the management of Adamus Resources for engaging constructively throughout the process. The Chamber further urged all parties involved to remain committed to the agreed roadmap and ensure that its implementation is guided by transparency, accountability and a shared determination to return the mine to sustainable operations. It stressed the importance of addressing outstanding liabilities and mobilising the investment required to secure the long-term viability of the company. Support for sector growth The Chamber reiterated its readiness to support initiatives that protect investments, preserve jobs and promote responsible local participation in the mining sector. It added that strengthening the contribution of mining to national development remained a key priority. The latest development comes amid renewed efforts by government and industry stakeholders to enhance the performance of Ghana’s mining sector, which remains one of the country’s leading sources of export earnings, employment and foreign exchange. Industry observers say the successful implementation of the Adamus recovery plan could serve as an important test case for resolving disputes in the extractive sector through dialogue and cooperation while maintaining investor confidence.
